name: North Outlet Park
note: USACE Harlan County Lake park below the dam on the north side of the Republican River, reached from Republican City by Corps Road A (South Outlet is the separate park across the river). Primitive undesignated camping off a gravel loop in the trees: pick a spot with a fire ring and picnic table and pay at the self-pay vault; the Corps gives no rig length. --Claude
inclusion_evidence: USACE Kansas City District Harlan County Lake Campgrounds page (live page 403; Wayback capture 2026-02-09, read 2026-11-05): 'Gremlin Cove, North and South Outlets and Cedar Point Park offers more basic experiences to campers ... select a campsite denoted by the presence of a fire ring and picnic table ... self-pay vault', fee list 'North and South Outlet - $12.00' + USACE North Outlet Park page (UNT End-of-Term archive 2009-01-09, read 2026-11-05): 'located on the north side of the Republican River below the dam. Water, refuse collection and 2 vault toilets ... Camping fees ... self-pay station' + Google Maps 'North Outlet Park' 40.07418,-99.20926, 4.5 on 31 reviews, not marked closed (gm.py 2026-11-05) + The Dyrt review Sep 2021 (N I., July visit): primitive, no designated sites, $12, FCFS, fire rings, drinking water, pit toilets + Esri Wayback 2015-08-15 GE01 z19 frame showing a white travel trailer (~10 m) with a tow vehicle parked on the gravel pad at the pin -> real USACE primitive drive-in RV campground on a gravel loop (not beach sand). Separate place from 2762 South Outlet: opposite bank of the river, its own road system from the north, a separate named USACE park. Public (federal): no price gate.
waterfront_evidence: 2026-11-05: Esri World Imagery (current 2025-08-16 LG01, rendered, 400 m / 440 m / 1.4 km / 3.2 km frames) and Esri Wayback 2010/2015/2021 z18-z19 (rendered) at 40.07418,-99.20955: the park sits in trees north of an irrigation canal (~10 m, concrete-lined), then a gravel road, a treeline and a brushy floodplain before the Republican River outlet channel ~350 m south; nothing at the sites is on or in view of open water. Below the dam: the spillway/stilling basin is ~350 m SW; the camping pad is 586 m on Open-Meteo DEM vs the lake's 593 m normal pool (1,946 ft, USACE map) and on the downstream side of the dam axis -> no lake value; river too far and screened for riverview -> not waterfront.

fees.note: $12 a night (USACE campground fee list, captured February 2026); paid at the self-pay vault or to rangers on patrol.

fees_source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260209025136/https://www.nwk.usace.army.mil/Locations/District-Lakes/Harlan-County-Lake/Campgrounds/, read 2026-11-05: 'Campground Fees ... Gremlin Cove Park - $14.00 North and South Outlet - $12.00 Cedar Point - $12.00'; 'Fees at these parks collected by park rangers on patrol the use of a self-pay vault.' One class only (basic camping); fee shape copied from 15617 Cedar Point / 2762 South Outlet.

booking.note: Self-pay vault; undesignated sites marked by a fire ring and table.

booking_source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260209025136/https://www.nwk.usace.army.mil/Locations/District-Lakes/Harlan-County-Lake/Campgrounds/ (reservations named only for Methodist Cove and Hunter Cove; the Outlets are 'select a campsite ... self-pay vault'); no North Outlet facility in RIDB rec area 264 (per the Cedar Point vetter, 2026-11-05); read 2026-11-05
flags: Duplicate check: nearest entries are 2762 South Outlet (pin 688 m S; its gravel lot at ~40.0703,-99.2092 is ~450 m S across the river), 2756 Gremlin Cove (1.27 km), 2757 Hunter Cove (1.9 km), 15617 Cedar Point (2.8 km). That is UNDER the ~1 km guide, but I counted North Outlet as a separate place: USACE ran them as two named parks with their own pages (2009: North Outlet 'on the north side of the Republican River below the dam', South Outlet 'on the south side'), the river runs between them with no bridge on imagery, and each has its own roads (North from Corps Road A / Republican City down the dam's downstream toe; South from the county road to the south up the dam toe). RV Life lists only South Outlet (objectID 256121, 60 sites); 2762's inclusion_evidence and pin cover the south field only. If AWH reads the 1 km guide strictly, this becomes a skip as a duplicate of 2762.

Pin: the gravel/sand pad on the NW side of the park's gravel loop, where the 2015-08-15 GE01 frame shows a white travel trailer and a tow vehicle; Google's 'North Outlet Park' point (40.07418,-99.20926) is 25 m E. A picnic shelter pad sits just W of it; the Dyrt reviewer's GPS (40.072998,-99.210250, typo'd as -90) is the park's SW corner by the dam-toe road.

Ignore The Dyrt's second page 'north-outlet-harlan-county-lake' (24 sites, 30-ft max, showers, archery range, boat ramp, on the lake): its reviewer GPS 40.086231,-99.213833 is at Gremlin Cove/North Shore, so it describes a different park. No rig length is used from it.
Rig fit: the Corps gives no length (silent) -> keep. Imagery shows a ~10 m travel trailer on the pad (2015); not put in sites.max_rig_ft.

Structured data for stamping: hookups electric 0 / water false / sewer false (2026 USACE page: the Outlets are 'more basic experiences' vs the 'sites with utilities' at Methodist/Hunter Cove; no pedestals on imagery); sites.count unknown (undesignated); pull_through none; booking reservable false, fcfs always, platform none (2026 USACE page); max_stay_nights 14 is the Corps-wide 36 CFR 327.7(a) rule if wanted (2762 carries it); facilities: vault_toilets true ('2 vault toilets', USACE 2009 page; 'pit toilets', Dyrt 2021), potable_water true ('Water ... located within this park', USACE 2009; 'drinking water', Dyrt 2021 - both old-ish, so stamp with care), trash dumpsters (2026 USACE page 'trash dumpsters provided in each park'), playground (Dyrt 2021; corpslakes table per the Cedar Point vetter), 1.5-mile nature trail at the east end (USACE 2009); dump not stated (leave absent); season: Dyrt 2021 reviewer says 'May-Sep', not on the USACE page (the May-October line is for Methodist and Hunter Cove designated sites) - leave season absent.
Fee history: $8 in 2009 (USACE page), $12 in the Feb 2026 capture.
